主要内容: The House passed the $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan, aimed at delivering financial relief to struggling families and ramping up vaccination distribution. The bill includes funding for vaccine production and distribution, another round of stimulus payments for many households, an extension of federal unemployment benefits, and more. The plan also introduces a fully refundable child tax credit for 2021, increasing the amount from $2,000 to $3,000 per child ages 6 to 17 and to $3,600 for children under the age of 6. The bill includes $30 billion in emergency rental assistance and an additional $5 billion to prevent Covid-19 outbreaks among homeless populations. It also earmarks $10 billion for mortgage assistance. The minimum wage increase to $15 per hour by 2025 was one of the most controversial provisions in the drafting of the bill. The House's $1.9 trillion American Rescue Plan includes provisions for a third economic impact payment, worth up to $1,400 per individual and dependent. The payments phase out gradually, hitting $0 for individuals earning an AGI over $100,000 per year and couples earning over $200,000 per year. The bill also extends key unemployment programs past their current March 14 expiration date through August 29, boosting enhanced federal payments from an extra $300 per week to $400. Additionally, the bill allocates $20 billion to create a national Covid-19 vaccination program and an additional $50 billion for virus testing. The American Rescue Plan also provides funding for schools, restaurants and bars, state and local aid, vaccine production and distribution, and paid leave. The Senate will likely pass a different version of the bill, and Democrats hope to have Biden sign the legislation by March 14.
